statement: The function returns a result r such that: (a) len(r[p]) = 3 for every p with 0 <= p < len(r); (b) for all p, q with 0 <= p < q < len(r), r[p] is not a permutation of r[q]; (c) for every multiset M of three integers, some element of r has M as its multiset of entries if and only if the three elements of M sum to 0 and there exist pairwise distinct indices i, j, k with 0 <= i, j, k < len(nums) and {nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]} = M.
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 3000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every element of r has exactly three entries: for every p with 0 <= p < len(r), len(r[p]) = 3.
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 3000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every triplet in r sums to zero: for every p with 0 <= p < len(r), r[p][0] + r[p][1] + r[p][2] = 0.
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 3000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every element of r is realized by three pairwise distinct positions of nums: for every p with 0 <= p < len(r) there exist indices i, j, k with 0 <= i, j, k < len(nums), i, j, k pairwise distinct, such that nums[i] = r[p][0], nums[j] = r[p][1] and nums[k] = r[p][2].
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 3000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, no two returned triplets have the same multiset of values: for all p, q with 0 <= p < q < len(r), the multiset {r[p][0], r[p][1], r[p][2]} differs from the multiset {r[q][0], r[q][1], r[q][2]}; equivalently, r[p] is not a permutation of r[q].
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 3000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every zero-sum triple of values taken at pairwise distinct positions of nums occurs in r: for all pairwise distinct i, j, k with 0 <= i, j, k < len(nums) and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] = 0, there exists p with 0 <= p < len(r) such that the multiset {r[p][0], r[p][1], r[p][2]} equals the multiset {nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]}.
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 3000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) equals the number of distinct multisets M of three integers such that the three elements of M sum to 0 and there exist pairwise distinct indices i, j, k with 0 <= i, j, k < len(nums) and {nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]} = M.
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 3000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r on every input satisfying the preconditions; it never fails, i.e. it does not panic, does not perform an out-of-bounds access, and does not overflow 64-bit arithmetic.
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 3000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.
